video_title: What If Lower Volatility Is the Wrong Goal | Open Interest | Ep.25
gist: Quantedge CEO Suhaimi Zainul Abidin explains how the ~$8B Singapore systematic fund harvests risk premia across ~300 markets plus insurance-linked securities, deliberately targeting ~25% volatility instead of the institutional 8-12% norm. He argues low volatility leaves return on the table, that total risk (vol, tails, correlation, margin, liquidity) and lockups/perpetual share classes are what make a levered strategy survivable, and cites a 29% March 2020 loss as the defining stress test.

insights.claim: Quantedge was founded in Singapore in 2006 by two non-finance founders (a statistics professor and a reinsurance pricing actuary) with about $3 million, and now manages close to $8 billion.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Outsider, first-principles quant backgrounds (stats + actuarial) shaped a risk-premium-harvesting design rather than a trend-following one.
insights.quote: managed to attract a grand total of about $3 million

insights.claim: Quantedge nearly doubled its fund in 2006-2007, lost almost half in 2008 to return roughly to its starting point, recovered to a new high in 2009, and posted its best-ever year in 2010 at about 82%.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Shows the path-dependence of a high-vol strategy: deep drawdowns followed by rapid recoveries.
insights.quote: 2010 was a was a blockbuster year for the fund, the highest return ever at about 82%

insights.claim: Quantedge has compounded at roughly 20% annualized over about 20 years, growing AUM about 4x per decade on average.
insights.speaker: Moritz Seibert (host) / Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: High-vol, levered multi-premia approach has delivered equity-beating compounding for two decades.
insights.quote: 4x is is something that we kind of achieve on average every 10 years

insights.claim: Quantedge's 2019 net return was about 70%, with more than half of it coming from bonds.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Return sources rotate sharply year to year in a dynamic allocation system.
insights.quote: more than half the returns, came from bonds

insights.claim: Most of Quantedge's 2026 returns came from market-neutral strategies in commodities, with directional energy commodities also performing very well.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Commodity relative-value and energy were the standout premia in 2026 for a large systematic multi-strategy fund.
insights.quote: most of our returns have come from market neutral strategies in the commodity space

insights.claim: Quantedge credits the strong equity decade for a fair amount of its profits, but says no single factor dominates returns because allocations shift with signal strength.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Avoid attributing a diversified premia fund's success to one style; allocation dynamism is the edge.

themes.theme: Risk premia as insurance: the core philosophy

insights.claim: Quantedge defines a risk premia strategy as accepting risk in exchange for expected return, analogous to an insurer charging above fair value for risk others want to offload.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Frames every market as a place to be paid for warehousing risk others want to shed.
insights.quote: A risk premia strategy is one which accepts risk essentially in exchange for uh an expected return.

insights.claim: Suhaimi argues most markets exist for the purpose of risk transfer, and that taking that risk (equity, bond, commodity) deserves a return the market adjusts to provide.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Underpins a strategy of harvesting premia across all asset classes rather than forecasting.
insights.quote: In fact, we think most markets exist for the purpose of risk transfer

insights.claim: Quantedge describes itself not as a trend follower/CTA but as systematic global macro whose core is market risk premia layered with long-short factor-based market-neutral strategies, essentially a capital-efficiency vehicle.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Allocators should bucket it as multi-premia/factor rather than trend following.
insights.quote: the core of it would be risk premia and factor-based market-neutral strategies

insights.claim: Suhaimi says periodic large losses are intrinsic to risk premia: investors get paid precisely because they bear the risk and occasionally take the hit.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Drawdowns are the cost of premium, not evidence of strategy failure.
insights.quote: you get paid out exactly because you're willing to bear that risk and from time to time take the hit

themes.theme: Insurance-linked securities as a niche premium

insights.claim: Quantedge invests in insurance-linked securities (cat bonds etc.), where it expects potentially around 20% returns over cash in some years and over the long term.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: ILS offers equity-like-plus, largely uncorrelated returns for those who can access it.
insights.quote: you could get potentially 20% uh, returns on cash

insights.claim: After catastrophe losses, capital drains from the ILS market the following year and premiums rise a lot, so consistent investors who stay through losses capture the higher subsequent yields.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Post-catastrophe years are the best entry points for reinsurance-style risk; staying power is the edge.
insights.quote: you will see that capital drains out of the market the following year. But as a result of that, actually the premiums go up a lot

insights.claim: Quantedge's ILS process is systematic only in deal analysis and risk-budget allocation; access is bespoke and negotiated deal by deal with cedents, with diversification across hurricane, earthquake, wildfire, cyber and satellite perils.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: ILS is a private, access-constrained market where sourcing matters as much as models.
insights.quote: We have to go to cedents and counterparties and negotiate deal by deal essentially.

insights.claim: ILS is under 10% of Quantedge's total risk because it is fully funded via a trust account and consumes cash, so it cannot be scaled up as much as the firm would like.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Capital-inefficiency (full collateralization) caps ILS sizing even when returns are attractive.
insights.quote: It takes up maybe about uh slightly less than 10% of total risk.

insights.claim: The host characterizes cat bond returns (e.g., the Swiss Re Cat Bond Index) as spectacular but negatively skewed, akin to being short an uncovered put.
insights.speaker: Moritz Seibert (host)
insights.so_what: Size ILS as a short-volatility/tail exposure, not as a bond substitute.

insights.claim: Quantedge deliberately targets about 25% volatility, far above the 8-12% range favored by institutional allocators.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge) / Moritz Seibert (host)
insights.so_what: Challenges the institutional preference for low-vol products; lower vol may leave return on the table.
insights.quote: we think that 25% is probably the right balance

insights.claim: Suhaimi argues that continually adding uncorrelated strategies to drive volatility down leaves risk on the table, so a diversified portfolio should be levered up to a higher risk level rather than kept at low volatility.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Diversification's payoff should be taken as higher levered return, not just lower vol.
insights.quote: Am I just leaving leaving risk on the table? Could I be taking more risk and as a result getting higher returns?

insights.claim: Volatility is not the most damaging measure of risk; at very high leverage the binding constraint is the chance of catastrophic loss, which is why Quantedge caps its target at around 25%.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Risk of ruin, not vol, sets the leverage ceiling.
insights.quote: volatility is only one measure of risk. It's not the most damaging measure of risk.

insights.claim: Quantedge sizes positions on 'total risk', combining volatility, tail risk, correlations, margin requirements and market liquidity, having moved beyond standard vol targeting after March 2020.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Leverage-using managers should treat margin and liquidity changes as risk inputs, not just vol.
insights.quote: there's volatility, there's tail risk, there's correlations, margins, and and liquidity

insights.claim: Quantedge's average margin-to-equity ratio in normal markets is around 30-40%.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Indicates substantial leverage supporting the 25% vol target.
insights.quote: Our average margin to equity ratio in normal market conditions would be around 30 to 40%.

insights.claim: Even naturally uncorrelated bets (e.g., interest rates vs. wildfires) occasionally fall together, so a levered high-risk portfolio must stay cognizant of correlated tail events.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Correlation spikes are the key threat to levered diversified portfolios.

insights.claim: Quantedge trades close to 300 markets, including 40+ equity indices, about 20 equity markets on a long-short single-stock basis, and 40-50 commodities, up from 50-plus markets at inception.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Breadth of independent bets is the engine of risk-adjusted return.
insights.quote: we list down uh close to about 300 different markets that we're in at any point in time

insights.claim: Suhaimi argues equity markets are substantially positively correlated with each other, so commodities (energy vs. agriculture/grains) are a far more powerful diversifier than adding more equity markets.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Investors claiming diversification via equities alone are under-diversified; commodities add real independence.
insights.quote: commodities is a huge diversifying sort of asset class for us

insights.claim: In early 2026 Quantedge moved from rebalancing once a day (since inception) to three times a day, re-sizing on risk and reallocating on changing signal attractiveness, which it says has worked well.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Higher rebalance frequency makes a levered premia book more reactive to fresh data.
insights.quote: today we we rebalance three times a day

insights.claim: Quantedge added long-short factor strategies in roughly the last 5 years and has rewritten the founders' models; Suhaimi says the original strategies could not manage $8 billion.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Scaling requires continuous strategy transformation, not just more capital in the original models.
insights.quote: I don't think that the original models, the original strategies would be able to manage $8 billion today.

insights.claim: Quantedge organizes research by signal type (enterprises/single stocks, rates, macro risk premia, plus a small ILS team) rather than by country, with about 130 staff of whom roughly a third do research and trading.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Signal-type organization supports a unified systematic process across 300 markets with a lean team.

insights.claim: Quantedge estimates its capacity at $30-35 billion, roughly 4x current AUM, and is investing resources now to push capacity higher, but says it will not take money that dilutes returns.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: At its historical growth rate the fund could approach capacity within about a decade, possibly sooner.
insights.quote: We think the fund capacity should be, you know, north of 30 billion, right? 30 to 35 billion.

insights.claim: Quantedge refuses requests for SMAs or separate vehicles with more liquidity or lower volatility, choosing to run a single fund on its own terms rather than bending to institutional allocators.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Single-product focus and alignment are prioritized over asset gathering.

insights.claim: Quantedge closed its monthly-liquidity share class in 2018 and now offers only 3- and 5-year fixed-term and semi-perpetual/perpetual classes; it says it launched these a month or two before Millennium's 5-year locked class.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Large hedge funds are moving toward long lockups to match capital to strategy horizons.
insights.quote: we offered monthly liquidity up to 2018 and then we closed that share class

insights.claim: Most of Quantedge's AUM sits in semi-perpetual (redeem up to 5% of shares per quarter) and perpetual classes; the perpetual class, limited to employees and very early investors, forms the fund's permanent capital base.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Endowment-like capital structure effectively eliminates run risk for a high-vol strategy.
insights.quote: they can withdraw or redeem up to 5% of their shares every quarter

insights.claim: Suhaimi argues a main reason funds close is a mismatch between strategy requirements and investors' ability to hold through tough periods, and that Quantedge's lockups have effectively eradicated the risk of a run on the fund.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Liquidity terms are a structural part of strategy survival, not just a commercial detail.
insights.quote: one of the main reasons is because there's a mismatch between the requirements of the strategy and the investor base

insights.claim: Despite saying they can handle volatility, investors get nervous in their first 20-30% drawdown and some redeem at the wrong time, which is why Quantedge locks up all of its nearly 1,000 investors.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Behavioral redemption risk justifies lockups even for liquid-market strategies.
insights.quote: when you get that 20 30% drawdown, I mean, everyone gets nervous

insights.claim: The host argues that at 25% volatility a 50% drawdown is only two standard deviations and does not mean the strategy is broken, but investors quitting mid-drawdown destroys compounding.
insights.speaker: Moritz Seibert (host)
insights.so_what: Investors in high-vol strategies must plan for 3-5 year rough patches to realize the CAGR.

insights.claim: Suhaimi says the best-performing Quantedge investors leave capital to grow 5-10x before drawing down, creating a large perpetual cash flow.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Time in the strategy, not timing, drives investor outcomes.

insights.claim: Quantedge's worst monthly drawdown was about 29% in March 2020, which Suhaimi calls more stressful than 2008 because losses were compressed into consecutive days amid lockdowns and counterparty demands.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Speed of drawdown, not just depth, is the real operational stress for levered funds.
insights.quote: where we lost uh 29%

insights.claim: After March 2020 Quantedge moved to total-risk targeting, rebalanced more frequently, expanded long-short strategies, and negotiated better broker terms so counterparties could not 'yank us around' in a crisis.
insights.speaker: Suhaimi Zainul Abidin (CEO, Quantedge)
insights.so_what: Counterparty/financing terms are a key resilience lever for leveraged systematic funds.
insights.quote: negotiated better terms with our brokers to make sure they can't yank us around in times of crisis
